title: Gambling Managers
description: Plan, direct, or coordinate gambling operations in a casino. May formulate house rules.

tasks.text: Monitor staffing levels to ensure that games and tables are adequately staffed for each shift, arranging for staff rotations and breaks and locating substitute employees as necessary.
Record, collect, or pay off bets, issuing receipts as necessary.
Circulate among gaming tables to ensure that operations are conducted properly, that dealers follow house rules, or that players are not cheating.
Track supplies of money to tables and perform any required paperwork.
Set and maintain a bank and table limit for each game.
Establish policies on issues, such as the type of gambling offered and the odds, the extension of credit, or the serving of food and beverages.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Resolve customer complaints regarding problems, such as payout errors.
Remove suspected cheaters, such as card counters or other players who may have systems that shift the odds of winning to their favor.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Explain and interpret house rules, such as game rules or betting limits.
Prepare work schedules and station arrangements and keep attendance records.
Direct the compilation of summary sheets that show wager amounts and payoffs for races or events.
Maintain familiarity with all games used at a facility, as well as strategies or tricks employed in those games.
Train new workers or evaluate their performance.
Review operational expenses, budget estimates, betting accounts, or collection reports for accuracy.
Market or promote the casino to bring in business.
Direct the distribution of complimentary hotel rooms, meals, or other discounts or free items given to players, based on their length of play and betting totals.
Notify board attendants of table vacancies so that waiting patrons can play.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Calendar and scheduling software
skills.def: Software to plan or organize the activities of a person or group. Examples: Employee scheduling software.
